Every other crossing on this map assumes a person carries the change. Native requires two conditions: durable state keyed to the world rather than to a participant, and a defined mechanism by which an external event mutates it while nobody is connected. Player-keyed persistence alone scores none on this row.

commerce.tooltip: Commerce and payments covers paying for things across a boundary and proving what was bought or granted. Payment is the exchange itself; entitlement is the check at the moment of use; a receipt is the portable record of a purchase or grant. Granted authority, network admission and a payment settlement are separate facts, so a subject can reach one without the others. A payment receipt is not a quality verdict, and a licence declaration is not an enforcement test.

The grant binds holder to resource and states expiry, revocation and transfer. Owning a record in an inventory is not the same as a grant another system can check, and declaring a licence is not enforcing it.

logic.agent-authoring.tooltip: This row asks whether an AI agent, working from outside, can build in a world or platform: create, change and publish its content through a documented interface such as an MCP server, a REST interface, a command line or a published instruction file. It is not the row for agents acting inside a world. An interface that exists only inside one editor's own tools, with no stated scope, does not meet the definition.

persist.world-export.tooltip: This row asks whether a whole place can leave its host: its scenes, assets, behaviour and settings exported and imported in open, documented files, with a statement of what survives if the host closes. Exporting single assets is a different row, and so is surviving a server restart. A download of raw files with no documented structure does not meet the definition.

sense.object-track.tooltip: This row asks whether a system recognises a known physical object from its three-dimensional model, with no markers or prepared images, and reports the object's pose so content stays fixed to it. Tracking printed markers or images is a different row. Recognising a general category of object, without the specific model, does not meet the definition.

render.remote.tooltip: This row records whether a system renders a view on a server from the device's predicted pose and streams the frames back for display. It is recorded descriptively: the Atlas notes which systems do it and does not define an agreement between client and renderer. Streaming ordinary video is a different row, because the view is not driven by the viewer's head.

net.live-data.tooltip: This row asks whether objects in a world can be bound to a live outside source, such as a sensor, a machine controller or a building system, so they follow the real asset, or so the real controller drives the simulated one. Importing a static snapshot of data does not meet the definition. Coupling two virtual worlds to each other is a different row.
